scope: Solid v1 UI library with explicitly named Solid Router and Solid Meta companions. SolidStart application features are reviewed in their own row.

ssr.note: renderToString produces synchronous HTML and hydration metadata.

streaming.note: renderToStream integrates Suspense fallback boundaries and streams their resolved content; the host must preserve flushing.

suspense.note: renderToStream integrates Suspense fallback boundaries and streams their resolved content; the host must preserve flushing.

client.note: hydrate attaches reactive behavior to SSR HTML; render creates a client application root.

ssg.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

csr.note: hydrate attaches reactive behavior to SSR HTML; render creates a client application root.

serverOnly.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

partialRendering.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

routing.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.
routing.label: Solid Router

layouts.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.
layouts.label: Solid Router

dynamicRoutes.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.

parallelRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

prefetch.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.
prefetch.label: Solid Router

softNavigation.note: Solid Router's delegated link handling and navigation primitives update route content and browser history without a full reload. Explicit link/reload controls determine which anchors are intercepted.
softNavigation.label: Solid Router

viewTransitions.note: The reviewed routing API does not establish this navigation capability. Application code or another package may provide it; this finding is not proof of absence.

redirects.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.
redirects.label: Solid Router

serverData.note: createResource tracks asynchronous reads with loading/error state and refetch/mutate controls; transport and persistent caching are separate.

clientData.note: createResource tracks asynchronous reads with loading/error state and refetch/mutate controls; transport and persistent caching are separate.

requestDedupe.note: Solid Router provides nested routes, parameters, navigation/preload helpers, cached queries and query revalidation.
requestDedupe.label: Solid Router

persistentCache.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

invalidation.label: Solid Router

isr.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

apiRoutes.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

httpErrors.note: The reviewed renderer does not own the HTTP response. The host server must select 404/5xx, map routing/render failures, and decide when headers are committed. Displaying an error or fallback in rendered HTML does not establish the HTTP status.
httpErrors.label: HTTP host required

actions.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

forms.note: Solid Router actions integrate HTML forms, parsed submission arguments, pending/error state and query revalidation. Input validation remains application code or a schema library. A no-JavaScript server submission also requires a server integration such as SolidStart.
forms.label: Solid Router actions

middleware.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

cookies.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

cssModules.note: The documented Vite/CSS Modules setup supplies local class names; Solid's runtime does not compile CSS itself.
cssModules.label: CSS Modules / Vite

scopedCss.note: The documented Vite/CSS Modules setup supplies local class names; Solid's runtime does not compile CSS itself.
scopedCss.label: CSS Modules / Vite

tailwind.note: The guide configures the separately installed Tailwind compiler.
tailwind.label: Tailwind

cssInJs.note: Macaron is a separately installed compile-time CSS-in-JS integration.
cssInJs.label: Macaron

images.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

fonts.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

scripts.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

assetPipeline.note: Solid’s UI runtime does not itself version image, CSS, or script URLs. Use a separate bundler such as Vite or the SolidStart application framework for a processed asset graph; literal URLs still need a deliberate cache policy.
assetPipeline.label: Build tool required

staticAssets.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

metadata.note: Solid Meta provides reactive Title, Meta and Link components under MetaProvider, including server collection and client navigation updates.
metadata.label: Solid Meta

dynamicMetadata.note: Solid Meta provides reactive Title, Meta and Link components under MetaProvider, including server collection and client navigation updates.
dynamicMetadata.label: Solid Meta

metadataInheritance.note: MetaProvider composes descendant head components. The reviewed guide does not establish a general nested object merge/reset contract for inherited SEO fields.
metadataInheritance.label: Component composition

metadataOverrides.note: MetaProvider composes descendant head components. The reviewed guide does not establish a general nested object merge/reset contract for inherited SEO fields.

cspNonce.note: Solid's server renderers accept a nonce for hydration scripts, but the host must generate it, set the policy and cover other inline sources. A supplied renderer nonce is less than automatic application-wide enforcement.
cspNonce.label: Renderer nonce option

csrf.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS security guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

environment.note: Build-tool environment conventions determine browser exposure. They do not create a server application boundary on their own.
environment.label: Build-tool boundary

types.note: Solid supplies TypeScript declarations and JSX typing; run the TypeScript compiler separately from bundling.

hmr.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidJS tooling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

unitTests.note: The guide documents Vitest with Solid Testing Library and Playwright for browser workflows; these are external test tools.

e2eTests.note: The guide documents Vitest with Solid Testing Library and Playwright for browser workflows; these are external test tools.

errorHandling.note: Solid ErrorBoundary catches rendering and reactive-update errors in its subtree and provides a fallback/reset function. It does not catch arbitrary event-handler or unrelated asynchronous callback failures; HTTP status handling is a separate concern.
errorHandling.label: Solid ErrorBoundary

serverHosting.note: These application/server responsibilities are outside the standalone Solid UI library. SolidStart and host libraries are reviewed separately.

subpathProxy.note: The reviewed UI library does not own production HTTP routing, asset mounting or reverse-proxy origin handling. A router/build tool and host framework must coordinate a subpath deployment; client-side route base support alone is not the complete server deployment contract.
subpathProxy.label: Host framework required

staticHosting.note: A browser build can be served as static files through its build tool. This does not provide request-time SSR or a static page-generation API.
staticHosting.label: Client build

xssEscaping.note: JSX text interpolation uses text output; innerHTML is a raw-HTML sink. Applications must sanitize untrusted content supplied to innerHTML.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: Progressive forms requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed UI API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.

optimisticUi.note: createResource.mutate supports a local optimistic value; application code owns confirmed-state reconciliation, failure rollback and overlapping mutations. This is weaker than an automatic mutation reconciliation contract.
optimisticUi.label: Resource mutate / app rollback

navigationBlocking.note: Solid Router useBeforeLeave runs before router navigation and can prevent, retry or cancel leaving. The application owns its prompt and dirty-state policy; this is not a universal custom dialog for browser unload or cross-origin navigation.
